novelty_flags.label: flagship completeness kernel
novelty_flags.one_line: The closest algorithmic comparator TikkaHyttinenKarvanen2021DoSearch is absent; its arbitrary-source do-calculus search with selection mechanisms must be compared explicitly to EXT-ID, including whether it can express the exact two-law input and why its completeness guarantee does not settle this problem.

soundness_flags.label: ass:response-interior
soundness_flags.one_line: A lower bound on every active atom of a response-function representation is not Kivva et al.'s observed-law positivity condition; retag it novel and justify it as a representation-indexed interior witness restriction.

soundness_flags.label: def:projective-row-space and thm:projective-nullspace-certificate
soundness_flags.one_line: Γ_M, a_v, b_t, and h depend on a chosen response-function representation and chosen U0, not on M alone; moreover strict positivity of u does not imply the asserted η/2 atom lower bound.

soundness_flags.label: def:source-influence-functions and thm:source-specific-limit
soundness_flags.one_line: D_SF and D_0F are declared on free multinomial coordinates but are multiplied by full one-hot residual vectors, so the influence functions require an explicit coordinate projection or an ambient derivative convention.

soundness_flags.label: prop:boundary-reductions
soundness_flags.one_line: Under the stated EXT-ID handle, T0=V produces no admissible nonempty margin-extension move and q0 is never stored as a population kernel, so reduction to ordinary ID from the full population law does not follow.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 3 / Open-ended Question 1
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Completeness is conditional on constructing a graph-compatible, response-interior margin-anchored hedge at every terminal EXT-ID failure.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: EXT-ID is sound and complete for the two-law recoverability problem conditional on a positive resolution of the margin-anchored hedge question.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 2747–2750, Definition 4, Algorithm 3, Theorem 4, and discussion immediately preceding Theorem 5
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Definition 4 uses P(V|S=1) and P(T0); Algorithm 3 takes exactly these two laws; Theorem 4 states IDSB is sound; the paper states it is unclear whether positive recoverable cases exist where IDSB returns FAIL.

The paper defines its positivity class by P_M(v)>0 for every observed cell and proves a sound-and-complete gID algorithm; it does not define the cited condition as a positive lower bound on active atoms of a finite response-function representation.

source_verification_receipts.version: UCLA Technical Report R-327, proceedings-matched AAAI 2006 version
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives a hedge criterion and a sound-and-complete ID algorithm for identification of P_x(Y) from one full observational distribution P(V).

The published paper studies systematic selection in multi-dataset causal inference with arbitrary unobserved confounding and supplies a general identification algorithm; its theorem-level comparison to the exact two-law model was not established from the accessible proceedings page.

do-search is a sound do-calculus search over arbitrary observational and experimental source distributions with selection mechanisms, and is complete only for identification problems already completely characterized by do-calculus.
This is a probability-class/potential-outcomes treatment of ATE identification from P(V|S=1), rather than arbitrary semi-Markovian graph recovery from a selected law plus an external margin.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add TikkaHyttinenKarvanen2021DoSearch to related work and state a precise separation theorem or audited counterexample showing that do-search does not provide the desired complete decision rule for the exact two-law input.
Replace Γ_M by a representation-indexed object Γ_(M,R,U0), require u_j≥η in the selected representation, and formulate the perturbation theorem over that fixed representation.
Specify EXT-ID's state, legal moves, branch ordering, and the direct T0=V initialization from q0=P(V), then re-prove all four boundary reductions against that precise algorithm.

Move the routine two-table delta-method and Bonferroni results to a clearly labeled supporting inference appendix unless the project develops the nonroutine graph-compatible tangent-space projection mentioned in the seed slate.

recommended_next_step: Revise the representation-dependent certificate and EXT-ID boundary specification, add the do-search comparison, then retain the completeness target as a conditional flagship kernel pending the three-node audit and margin-anchored hedge construction.
